The positive record is mostly indirect, institutional, or limited to specific sectors, while the negative record is broader and better documented.","evidence":[{"title":"2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Philippines","publisher":"U.S. Department of State","date":"2024","url":"https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128580.html","summary":"The report says the Marcos administration refocused the antidrug campaign toward treatment, due process, and rule-of-law-based investigations, which is the clearest official-signaled shift away from Duterte-style arbitrary violence.","question_ids":["3B.1"]},{"title":"Marcos bans POGOs, cites disorder it caused PH","publisher":"Philippine Daily Inquirer","date":"2024-07-23","url":"https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1964063/marcos-bans-pogo-cites-disorder-it-caused-ph","summary":"Marcos banned all POGOs after citing torture, kidnapping, human trafficking, and murder linked to the industry. This is a real protective step against severe abuse, though it is more about criminal exploitation than state violence.","question_ids":["3B.1"]},{"title":"Marcos announces ban on all POGO","publisher":"GMA News Online","date":"2024-07-22","url":"https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/914272/marcos-announces-ban-on-all-pogo/story/","summary":"Marcos framed the ban as stopping “grave abuse” and illegal acts, and ordered POGOs wound down by year-end. This supports a limited claim that he acted against a violent abuse network.","question_ids":["3B.1"]},{"title":"DOJ creates task force to review EJK cases","publisher":"Philippine News Agency","date":"2024-11-06","url":"https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1237266","summary":"The DOJ created a task force to investigate Duterte-era extrajudicial killings, build cases, and file charges if warranted. That is the strongest 2024 accountability move tied to state violence.","question_ids":["3B.1"]},{"title":"No PH cooperation with ICC unless PRRD wants it – PBBM","publisher":"Presidential Communications Office","date":"2024-11-14","url":"https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/no-ph-cooperation-with-icc-unless-prrd-wants-it-pbbm/","summary":"Marcos said domestic authorities would keep reviewing the drug-war record and the DOJ would continue reassessing testimonies and evidence. This is some accountability signaling, but it is narrowed by his refusal to cooperate with the ICC.","question_ids":["3B.1"]},{"title":"World Report 2025: Philippines","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2025-01-16","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2025/country-chapters/philippines","summary":"HRW says drug-war killings persisted in 2024, enforced disappearances continued, and the Marcos administration still refused to cooperate with the ICC. It also says police/security-force abuse remained a serious issue.","question_ids":["3B.1"]},{"title":"Philippines: “Submit and surrender”: the harms of arbitrary drug detention in the Philippines","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-11-28","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/asa35/8759/2024/en/","summary":"Amnesty documents arbitrary detention in drug “treatment and rehabilitation” centers, including torture, ill-treatment, and forced or unreliable confessions. This is relevant because it shows intimidation and coercive pressure remained part of the civic environment.","question_ids":["3B.1"]}]}
